newsitem.title: UK: Weak Atlantic grain demand undermines BFI.
newsitem.headline: Weak Atlantic grain demand undermines BFI.

text.p: Relatively poor demand in the Atlantic grain trades, especially for Panamaxes, has been largely responsible for the recent decline in the BFI which fell again today, down 13 points to 1483.

In contrast conditions for Capers remain buoyant worldwide and have cushioned the fall of the index. The performance of handy-sizes has been mixed but has continued to be poor in the US Gulf and S.Atlantic.
GRAIN - Caper/Panamax activity were limited and Oldendorff fixed the Cargill-relet Yick Jia 67,000 dwt to cover grain from Baltimore to the Far East but details were slow to emerge.

In addition to Ascona 64,942 dwt, Egyptian charterers are reported to have booked 2 more Panamaxes for grain from North France, Pamphilos 60,867 dwt delivery N.Spain redelivery Passero at $10,500 daily to MISR and El Hadjar 64,698 dwt on unknown terms to NNC.

Iranian charterers have also been seeking Panamax tonnage for grain from the EU but are not known to have covered this week. Brokers advise that early Feb Panamaxes are now indicating $12.75 to Cargill and $13.00 to Toepfer for heavy grain US Gulf/Continent against charterers' ideas of $12.00, and $24.75 no combination for US Gulf/Japan against $23.00/24.00.

Toepfer are rumoured to have fixed several January handy-sizes on private terms - about 1.2m cft US Gulf to Gibraltar-Hamburg, 20,000 tonnes 53' Paranagua/Continent in the region of $18.00, a Plate/Philippines (but no details), and 20,000 Hamburg/Libya at about $25.00.
Shipmair are said to have fixed Trade Will 43,841 dwt as well as a Panamax vessel E.C.South America/Continent. Brokers noted the absence of fresh chartering enquiry today.

MINERALS - Some impressive voyage and timecharter rates were reported today. Rohstoffhandel paid $7.15 for 100,000 iron ore Port Cartier/Rotterdam for mid Feb loading, and Rogesa booked Amber for 160,000 iron ore Ponta da Madeira/Rotterdam for Feb 1/14 at $5.80.

Coe and Clerici fixed Kalahari for 120,000 coal Hampton Roads/Prai Mole Jan/Feb loading at $5.85 earlier this week. Noble have taken 2 capers on subjects on timecharter for trips via Brazil to China - New Harvest 208,739 dwt delivery Continent early Feb at $18,000 daily and the ore carrier Rhodos 137,587 dwt delivery Dunkirk end Jan at $11,300 daily.

In the east Doric Chariot 73,350 dwt was fixed by NYK delivery Goa early Feb trip Japan aclose to $13,500 daily plus about $20,000 bonus, and Transworld 71,500 dwt was reported booked by MOSK delivery Hongkong end Jan for a trip via Queensland to Japan at $11,000/11,250 daily.

In the fertlizer trades the 1981-built Maria 61,400 dwt fixed and failed on subjects with Grand International delivery US Gulf prompt trip China at $12,100 daily plus $250,000 bonus. Stone Gemini was understood covered for 50,000 tonnes potash Ventspils/China for Jan 19/25 at $25.00.

Heraklia 65,159 dwt was linked with Halla delivery Japan Jan 25 for a Nopac round, and Torm Gerd 69,451 dwt was said to have been fixed from Singapore for an Atlantic round via Australia, but further details were lacking.

HANDY-SIZES - The Atlantic timecharter market was reasonably active but rates were generally flat. UBT fixed David Agmashenebeli 38,237 dwt delivery prompt Gibraltar for a trip via Puerto Ordaz and Murmansk redelivery passing Norway at $6,500 daily by UBT, and EAC booked A.Tsereteli 38,226 dwt delivery US Gulf trip Adriatic at $7,000 daily plus $170,000 bonus.

In the east Halla fixed a 37,000 dwt logger for 4-6 months at $7,500 daily, and Alberto Topic 43,473 dwt was rumoured fixed in direct continuation by Western Bulkcarriers basis prompt delivery Taiwan for about 2-5 months in the low $9,000's daily.
